cases.persona: Priya, freelancer, 25% set aside for tax (invented, FIN-20)
cases.situation: Priya is a freelancer with no scheduled pay. Over the last six months (April to September) her freelance work paid $4,100, $3,900, $4,000, $4,200, $3,800 and $4,000, always on the 1st; at setup she chose a steady amount of $4,000 a month. $4,000 came in on 1 October. By 10 October she has paid $1,500 of bills and spent $300; $2,200 is in her everyday account and $2,300 sits in her savings account marked as her safety net (locked, the default). She is looking at a $300 purchase, bought today (10 October 2026) and paid in one go. A usual month: bills $1,500 and everyday spending $1,000 ($800 of it on essentials). On the pay setup screen she typed that she puts 25% of her freelance pay aside for tax.
cases.why: FIN-20: freelance pay counts after the share she puts aside for tax. 25% of $4,000 is $1,000, so her steady month counts as $3,000, and $1,000 of the $4,000 that came in on 1 October is still in her everyday account but kept for tax, so the answer does not spend it. October without a set-aside: $4,000 in - $1,500 bills - $300 spent - $700 everyday still to come = $1,500 left; $1,500 - $300 = $1,200. With the set-aside: $3,000 in - $1,500 bills - $300 spent - $700 still to come = $500 left; $500 - $300 = $200. The tight floor is $250 (a tenth of $1,500 bills + $1,000 everyday spending), and $200 is under it, so the answer is "Fits, but tight" instead of a plain "Fits". Her safety net is exactly its starter size ($1,500 bills + $800 essentials = $2,300), so there are no extra savings above it. The fact line says: "$1,000 a month is kept aside for tax, the 25% you set." Her November pay counts at her lowest month less 25% ($3,800 - $950 = $2,850) on 1 November, the same day as her bills, so the cash path stays above $0.

cases.plannerNote: Drafted in 06.1-29 and approved as drafted. Plain calculator (withTaxSetAside) and the engine on the same set-aside world agree: fits_month, tight, month 20000. Without the set-aside both say fits_month, null, 120000.

cases.persona: Leo, salary plus freelance, 25% of the freelance part set aside (invented, FIN-20)
cases.situation: Leo is paid a $2,500 salary on the 1st and also does freelance work. His income types are salary and freelance. Over the last six months his freelance work paid $1,600, $1,400, $1,500, $1,700, $1,300 and $1,500, always on the 5th; at setup he chose a steady freelance amount of $1,500 a month. In October his $2,500 salary came in on the 1st and $1,500 of freelance pay on the 5th. He typed that he puts 25% of his freelance pay aside for tax. By 10 October he has paid $1,500 of bills and spent $300; $2,200 is in his everyday account and $2,300 sits in his savings account marked as his safety net (locked). He is looking at a $300 purchase, bought today (10 October 2026) and paid in one go. A usual month: bills $1,500 and everyday spending $1,000 ($800 of it on essentials).
cases.why: FIN-20: only the freelance part is reduced; the salary is unchanged. 25% of his $1,500 freelance pay is $375, so October counts $2,500 + $1,125 = $3,625 in, and $375 of the freelance pay that came in on 5 October stays in his account but kept for tax. $3,625 - $1,500 bills - $300 spent - $700 everyday still to come = $1,125 left; $1,125 - $300 = $825, over the $250 tight floor, so a plain "Fits". If the 25% were wrongly taken from his salary too ($1,000 off $4,000), he would have $200 left and the answer would be "Fits, but tight". The fact line says: "$375 a month is kept aside for tax, the 25% you set." Without the set-aside he would have $1,200 left.

cases.persona: Priya, freelancer, 60% set aside, the most allowed (invented, FIN-20)
cases.situation: Priya is a freelancer with no scheduled pay. Over the last six months (April to September) her freelance work paid $4,100, $3,900, $4,000, $4,200, $3,800 and $4,000, always on the 1st; at setup she chose a steady amount of $4,000 a month. $4,000 came in on 1 October. By 10 October she has paid $1,500 of bills and spent $300; $2,200 is in her everyday account and $2,300 sits in her savings account marked as her safety net (locked, the default). She is looking at a $300 purchase, bought today (10 October 2026) and paid in one go. A usual month: bills $1,500 and everyday spending $1,000 ($800 of it on essentials). On the pay setup screen she typed 60%, the most the field takes, for the share she puts aside for tax.
cases.why: FIN-20: 60% is the top of the range (the settings column holds 0% to 60%; the field takes no more). 60% of $4,000 is $2,400, so her steady month counts as $1,600, which is $900 less than her $2,500 of usual bills and everyday spending: her month is already short before the purchase. October: $1,600 in - $1,500 bills - $300 spent - $700 still to come = -$900; -$900 - $300 = -$1,200. Her safety net is locked and there is nothing above it, so the purchase cannot be covered and the answer is "Not yet", led by "your month is already short". The fact line says: "$2,400 a month is kept aside for tax, the 60% you set."

cases.persona: Ana, new freelancer on quick estimates, 25% set aside (invented, FIN-20)
cases.situation: Ana is a freelancer who started using the app three weeks ago, so she has no full month of records yet and no pay recorded. Her income type is freelance only, with no steady amount set. In her quick estimates she typed income of $3,000 a month, bills $1,200 and everyday spending $600 ($400 of it on essentials). On the pay setup screen she typed that she puts 25% of her freelance pay aside for tax. Besides the estimates, Decide counts what she has recorded: by 22 November she has paid $1,200 of bills and spent $440; $6,000 from earlier work is in her everyday account and $1,600 sits in her savings account marked as her safety net (locked, the default). She is looking at a $600 purchase, bought today (22 November 2026) and paid in one go.
cases.why: FIN-20 (owner 2026-11-12): with no pay recorded, the typed quick income estimate stands in for her pay, and with freelance ticked it is freelance pay, so it counts less the share she puts aside for tax. 25% of $3,000 is $750, so her month counts $2,250 in. Without the set-aside: $3,000 - $1,200 bills - $440 spent - $160 everyday still to come = $1,200 left; $1,200 - $600 = $600, a plain "Fits" from this month. With it: $2,250 - $1,200 - $440 - $160 = $450 left, so this month covers $450 of the $600 and the other $150 comes from the $6,000 of earlier money in her everyday account: "Fits from spare money" (this month is used up, $0 left). Nothing has come in yet, so nothing is held back from her account. The fact line says: "$750 a month is kept aside for tax, the 25% you set."
cases.ownerReason: Owner approved TX-16 (D-26, 2026-11-12, chat popup): the tax set-aside also comes off a typed quick income estimate when freelance is ticked. A one-check + income quick line is not cut; it counts as typed.
cases.plannerNote: Draft (06.1-29, owner asked 2026-11-12 for the set-aside on a typed quick income estimate). Plain calculator and engine agree: fits_unspent, null, month 0; without the set-aside both say fits_month, null, 60000. Only the estimate carries her income here (no pay series, no income line, no steady figure), so this case pins the estimate rule. Approved 2026-11-12; DECIDE_ENGINE_REVISION 06.5.
